section: Procedure for Enrollment of Old Students
content: PROCEDURE FOR ENROLLMENT OF OLD STUDENTS: 1. Log-in to OLEA for encoding of courses. 2. Select and click the Block Section button then Submit. 3. Check the approved study load by the College. 4. Decision: If eligible for token fee exemption, click 'Apply for Tuition/Token Fee Exemption' button and check approval from Center for Admission and Scholarship (CAS); or apply for Promissory note. 5. Check the details of the assessment in OLEA. 6. Log-in to UMak Scan-to-Pay using login credentials for OLEA. Enter desired amount, check payable amount, scan or download QR Code. 7. Pay total amount via GCash (iBayad) by scanning or uploading QR code. Download copy of payment/GCash reference. 8. Payment confirmation in UMak Scan-to-Pay: input GCash sim and reference number, amount paid, read statement and click confirm. Copy UMak Reference Number. 9. Download and print Certificate of Registration (COR) emailed by ITC.

section: Article III. Section 1. Residency Verification
content: ARTICLE III. POLICIES ON SCHOOL FEES AND OTHER FEES. The Accounting Office is in charge of verifying student's residency, assessment of school fees, payments and issuance of final permit. SECTION 1. RESIDENCY VERIFICATION: 1.1 The University of Makati prioritizes Makati residents during admission. Residency verification is applied for to determine the amount of token fee during enrollment. Residency Verification Form (RVF) from Accounting Office must be accomplished. 1.2 ExCom Resolution No. 2021-109 (March 18, 2021): Student-applicant classified as MAKATI RESIDENT if: Report Card from Makati public high school or Report Card from Makati non-public high school but parents are voters/residents of Makati; Voter's Certification of student-applicant; or Verification list/Certification from DepEd-Makati or Higher School ng UMak (HSU). For students 18 years old and above: Voter's Certificate from recent local/national elections. Notes: Included on DepEd-Makati or HSU list considered MAKATI resident for 1 academic year. Failure to submit classified as non-Makati resident. Any misrepresentation shall warrant expulsion.

section: Article III. Section 2. Assessment of School Fees
content: SECTION 2. ASSESSMENT OF SCHOOL FEES: Circular Ordinance No. 2012-061: Effective Academic Year 2012-2013, the University charges tuition/token fees. Log-in to https://umak.edu.ph/olea for assessment. 2.1 Undergraduate Program Token Fee: Makati Resident: Php 1,000.00; Non-Makati Resident: Php 3,000.00. Miscellaneous fee is based on year level and college. Organization Fees: Insurance (1st Sem only) Php 50.00; University Student Council Fee Php 50.00; University Student Media Group Php 50.00; Culture and the Arts Php 50.00; Organization Fee Php 50.00. 2.2 Graduate Program Token Fee: TCP Php 500.00 per unit; Masters Php 750.00 per unit; Doctorate Php 1,000.00 per unit. 2.3 Other Fees: Registration / Entrance Fee Php 50.00; University ID Fee (New) Php 50.00; University ID Fee (Replacement) Php 100.00; Completion Php 20.00; Form 137A Php 20.00; Transfer Credentials Php 20.00; Authentication Php 30.00.

section: Article III. Section 3. Policies on Payment
content: SECTION 3. POLICIES ON PAYMENT: 3.1 Issuance of Final Permit: Issued to students with no remaining balance every semester before final examination. 3.2 Terms of Payment: Tuition/token fee may be paid in full, partial or promissory note before schedule of final examination. 3.3 Mode of Payment: Payment of token and miscellaneous fee is done through GCash - iBAYAD after student inputs payment details to UMAK Scan-to-Pay. Registrar's Office and ITC will send Certificate of Registration (COR). 3.4 Promissory Note: Granted to students unable to pay tuition/token fees upon enrollment. Must pay miscellaneous fee; balance paid before final examination to qualify for final permit. 3.5 Refund on Tuition/Token Fee: Allowed only if subject/s enrolled is/are dissolved by college or overpayment with no remaining balance. Applied within one month from start of class. Requirements: letter request, printed copy of COR, original official receipt / GCash transaction receipt, photocopy of ID.

section: Article III. Section 4. Scholarship and Tuition/Token Fee Exemption
content: 3.6 Waive of Tuition/Token Fee Balance: Balance on current semester may be waived if student filed Leave of Absence (LOA) within one month from start of class, or if LOA filed due to medical reasons. Requirements: Clearance, Approved LOA, Medical Certificate. SECTION 4. SCHOLARSHIP AND TUITION/TOKEN FEE EXEMPTION: Full and partial exemptions from payment of tuition/token fee awarded provided: Minimum requirements are met; Regular study load prescribed in curriculum is carried; Tuition/Token fee for semester applied for is NOT yet paid. The four types of scholarships granted by University of Makati are classified as: 1) academic, 2) achievement, 3) special, and 4) government/private/NGOs. 4.1 ACADEMIC: 4.1.1 Dean's Lister Token Fee Exemption Grant. Requirements: Filled out application form, Report of Grades during previous semester.

section: Article III. Section 4.1 - 4.3 Scholarships
content: 4.1.2 Entrance Token Fee Exemption Grant: Awarded to incoming freshmen who graduated Senior High School with High Honor (partial exemption) or Highest Honor (full exemption). 4.1.3 Maritime Scholarship: Full token fee exemption for undergraduate students of College of Maritime Leadership Innovation (CMLI). 4.2 ACHIEVEMENT: Band Member, Chorale, Corps of Sponsors, Dance Troupe, Naval Reserve Officer Training Corps (NROTC) Cadet Officer, PEP Squad, Theater Artist, University Student Council (USC) Officer, Varsity Player. Requirements: Filled-out application form, Endorsement from Head of concerned Office, Report of Grades. 4.3 SPECIAL: Cooperating Teachers Graduate Program, Displaced Needy Students from Marawi, Makati Barangay Chairman/Kagawad and Legitimate Dependents or Sangguniang Kabataan Chairman/Kagawad, Employees of the City Government of Makati and Makati Public School Teachers, Senior Citizens.

section: Article III. Section 4.4 Government/Private/NGO Scholarships
content: 4.3.6 Makati in Need of Educational Scholarship (MINES - continuing applicants only); 4.3.7 Makati Training Placement and Livelihood Consortia (MTPLC); 4.3.8 Persons With Disability (PWD) as per R.A. 9442 Magna Carta for Disabled Persons; 4.3.9 Dependents of Military Personnel; 4.3.10 Sister City; 4.3.11 UMak Teaching and Non-Teaching Employees and Dependents. 4.4 GOVERNMENT/PRIVATE/NON-GOVERNMENT ORGANIZATIONS (NGOs) SCHOLARSHIPS: Open to students in four-year degree programs not enjoying other token fee exemption benefits. Both Makati and non-Makati residents may apply. Partner organizations: 4.4.1 Cebuana Lhuillier Foundation, Inc.; 4.4.2 Luis Co Chi Kiat Foundation, Inc. (LCCKFI); 4.4.3 Rotary Club of Makati West; 4.4.4 University of Makati Employees Multipurpose Cooperative (UMEMPC); 4.4.5 Real Life Foundation, Inc.

section: Procedure for Issuance of Final Permit
content: PROCEDURE FOR ISSUANCE OF FINAL PERMIT: 1. Student initiates Online Application of Final Permit. 2. Verification of fee settlement and compliance. 3. If complied: Approved Final Permit. If not complied: Disapproved Final Permit. 4. Student logs in to UMak email. 5. If approved: Save and Print the Final Permit. If disapproved: Comply all requirements and reapply.

section: Procedure for Application of Scholarship / Token Fee Exemption
content: PROCEDURE FOR APPLICATION OF SCHOLARSHIP/TUITION/TOKEN FEE EXEMPTION: 1. Student Online Application through OLEA: Student clicks 'Apply for Tuition/Token Fee Exemption' button after saving class schedule. 2. Student chooses type of tuition/token exemption qualified for and clicks 'submit'. 3. Student checks inbox/spam folder of official UMak email for pre-filled form and submission link. 4. Student fills out Google form and submits complete scanned requirements for evaluation by Center for Admission and Scholarship (CAS). 5. CAS Head/Staff approves or disapproves: if approved, CAS grants application through OLEA. 6. Student logs in to OLEA and accesses Scan-to-Pay.

section: Article IV. Section 1 & 2. Academic Status & Probation
content: ARTICLE IV. ACADEMIC-ADMINISTRATIVE POLICIES. SECTION 1. CLASSIFICATION OF STUDENTS: Classified by curriculum year: First Year (1st & 2nd Sem), Second Year, Third Year, Fourth Year, Fifth Year. SECTION 2. ACADEMIC STATUS: 2.1 Good Standing: Obtained passing grades in ALL enrolled courses. Additional retention rules may be imposed by specific colleges. 2.2 Probationary Status or 'at risk student': Students who at end of semester obtain failing grades in TWO (2) of their enrolled courses (equivalent to less than 9 units). Action: 1. Academic intervention: Report to College Dean for academic intervention (deloading of courses, dedicated monitoring, tutorials, transfer). 2. Guidance Counseling: Report to Guidance Office to support academic success. Probationary status lifted as soon as grade requirements for Good Standing are met.

section: Article IV. Section 2.3 & 4. Academic Delinquency & Residency
content: 2.3 Academic Delinquency: 2.3.1 Students who obtain three (3) failing grades equivalent to 9 units. 2.3.2 Students who have accumulated five (5) failing grades (5.0) equivalent to 15 units during various semesters of stay. 2.3.3 Students who have accumulated five Unofficially Dropped (U.D.) marks equivalent to 15 units. Action: Barred from enrollment. Disqualified permanently from enrollment. Transfer credentials released upon request. Guidance Office conducts exit interview. Maximum Residency Exception: 4th year students are immune from disqualification but subject to Maximum Residence Rule (MRR) of one (1) year. SECTION 3. ACADEMIC EXCLUSION. SECTION 4. RESIDENCY: Baccalaureate programs have maximum residence of 5 years to finish degrees. One year extension granted to working students or students who filed LOA for not more than 2 semesters with Dean's approval.

section: Article IV. Section 5 & 6. LOA and Academic Load
content: SECTION 5. LEAVE OF ABSENCE (LOA): 5.1 Student filing LOA must seek permission and approval from all teachers and College Dean. 5.2 Leaving without approved LOA will be denied readmission. SECTION 6. STUDENT ACADEMIC LOAD: 6.1 Regular load is reflected in curriculum. Block sectioning observed. 6.2 Minimum Load: 15 units for undergraduate courses. Underload below 15 units requires Dean's permission. 6.3 Overload of Graduating Students: 6.3.1 Overload must not exceed six (6) units in excess of normal load. 6.3.2 Graduating students with 28 units remaining academic load and very good record may be allowed overload up to 28 units (max overload 7 units). 6.3.4 Three laboratory courses (5 units per course) permitted if graduating and total load not exceeding 21 units. P.E. load for graduating students: up to four (4) units of P.E. allowed at one time with other courses (max 28 units total); in extreme cases, graduating students allowed up to eight (8) units of P.E.

section: Article IV. Section 7 & 8. CMAT and Withdrawal
content: SECTION 7. CHANGE OF MATRICULATION (CMAT): 7.1 Student may add or cancel course or transfer sections within prescribed period only. 7.2 Dropping of courses must be done not later than a week after the midterm examination. The student shall be marked Officially Dropped (O.D.). 7.3 Procedure: Access Online Change of Matriculation (OLCMAT: https://umak.edu.ph/olcmat/), click 'X' to drop or 'CAN BE ENROLLED' to add. Pay fee via umak.edu.ph/scantopay. Official CMAT Form emailed within 24 hours. SECTION 8. WITHDRAWAL OF CREDENTIALS AND ENROLLMENT: Proceed to Office of University Registrar for cancellation of all semestral courses and request Transfer Credentials.

section: Article IV. Section 9, 11 & 12. Shifting, Attendance & Exams
content: SECTION 9. POLICIES ON CHANGE OF PROGRAM/MAJOR (Shifting): 9.1 Shifting shall be approved by both releasing and accepting Colleges upon submission of student's letter of intent. 9.2 Changing of program permitted only on the first semester of the academic year. 9.3 Grades must qualify according to program standards. 9.4 Disqualified students advised to transfer to non-baccalaureate program. SECTION 11. POLICIES ON ATTENDANCE: A student is expected to attend all classes regularly. Anyone who incurs 20% (11 hours) of total hours of instruction may be given a failing grade if majority of absences are unexcused. If excused, student is given a dropped mark. SECTION 12. POLICIES ON EXAMINATION: Violations considered prima facie evidence of cheating: attempting to communicate, giving/receiving information, unauthorized textbooks/notes -> assigned grade of 5.0. Cheating during final examination punishable by suspension from University.

section: Article IV. Section 13. Policy on Grading System
content: SECTION 13. POLICY ON GRADING SYSTEM: Numerical Percentage & Adjectival Equivalent: 1.00 = 97-100% (Excellent); 1.25 = 94-96% (Superior); 1.50 = 91-93% (Superior); 1.75 = 88-90% (Very Good); 2.00 = 85-87% (Very Good); 2.25 = 82-84% (Good); 2.50 = 79-81% (Good); 2.75 = 76-78% (Fair); 3.00 = 75% (Fair / Passing); 4.00 = 74-70% (Conditional Failure); 5.00 = 69% and below (Failure); INC = Incomplete; OD = Officially Dropped; UD = Unofficially Dropped. SECTION 14. MARKS OF 4.0 OR CONDITIONAL FAILURE AND INC: Grade of 4.0 removed when student passes re-examination within five days after final examination period or before encoding of final grades. Passes -> 3.0; fails/unable to remove -> 5.0. Removal of INC in non-prerequisite course must be done within one year after incurred.

section: Article IV. Section 14.7 Procedure for Removal of INC
content: SECTION 14.7 Procedure for removal of INC: 14.7.1 Download Completion Form from UMak Website. 14.7.2 Fill out Completion Form. 14.7.3 Send requirements and accomplished form to professor's official UMak email, copy Department Chair. 14.7.4 Professor indicates requirement details, signs, and forwards to Department Chair. 14.7.5 Department Chair signs and forwards to Dean. 14.7.6 Dean signs and endorses to Registrar at registrar@umak.edu.ph. 14.7.7 University Registrar validates and processes completion grade, sends validated form to student and college. 14.7.8 College Secretary keeps file of email trail and Completion Form.

section: Article IV. Section 17. Retention in Professional Courses
content: SECTION 17. POLICIES ON RETENTION: 17.1.2 A student who fails twice in the same course in his professional program shall not be readmitted in the same program. 17.2 Professional Courses: 17.2.1 Student who fails twice in the same course in professional program shall not be readmitted in same program. 17.2.2 Third and fourth year students who fail in two major courses shall be advised to change field of specialization and allowed to register only not more than 15 units. 17.2.3 Failure in three major courses shall be barred from re-registration. 17.3 Students Appealing for Retention: 17.3.1 Only students with recommendations from respective Deans allowed to continue. 17.3.2 Retained students placed on probationary status: obtained GWA of 2.25 during 1st semester, no failing mark in any subjects, received 2.5 or better in previously failed courses.

section: Article IV. Section 18 & 19. Grade Appeal and Internship
content: SECTION 18. POLICIES ON ACADEMIC GRADE APPEAL: 18.1 Amendment of Grades (both student and faculty initiated). 18.2 Amendment of Grade/s or inclusion of name in Grade Sheets must be made within a year after issuance of Report of Grades (ROG), approved by Council of Deans and Directors. SECTION 19. POLICIES ON INTERNSHIP PROGRAMS: 19.1 Qualifications: Officially enrolled in internship course, completed majority of coursework/prerequisites, at least 18 years old. 19.2 Procedures: Pre-deployment orientation by CLCDP; Host Training Establishments (HTEs); documentation: recommendation/endorsement letter, Personal Information Sheet (PIS), Internship Agreement and Consent. Post-deployment: Rating Sheet, Certificate of Completion, Narrative Report.

section: Article IV. Section 20 & 21. Graduation, Honors and Awards
content: SECTION 20. POLICIES ON GRADUATION: Students expecting to graduate must apply for evaluation two months before end of term preceding semester of graduation. File official application with Registrar before midterm examinations. Requirements: Certificate of Registration, UMak ID card. SECTION 21. POLICIES ON HONORS AND AWARDS: GWA and Academic Award Scale: Baccalaureate Program: 1.0 - 1.15 Summa Cum Laude; 1.16 - 1.30 Magna Cum Laude; 1.31 - 1.45 Cum Laude. Non-Baccalaureate Program: 1.0 - 1.1 With Highest Honors; 1.16 - 1.30 With High Honors; 1.31 - 1.45 With Honors. Additional requirements: Provided there is no grade lower than 2.0 in any academic course; candidate completed 75% of total academic units in UMak; semester load according to curriculum and at no time less than 15 units; no 5.0, INC, OD, UD; NSTP courses not reflecting grade lower than 2.50.

section: Article IV. Section 23. Application for School Records
content: SECTION 23. PROCEDURE FOR APPLICATION FOR SCHOOL RECORDS: 23.1 Access Online Transactions and Request for Appointment System (OLTRA): https://umak.edu.ph/appointment and select 'Request' for Application for School Records. Enter Student No. and verify from email. Processing: 90 processing days, check email for claim stub. Purchase documentary stamps, pay fee at Cash Office, submit to Registrar, sign receiving logbook and check records.

section: Article V. Section 1. Academic Scholarships (Dean's Lister)
content: ARTICLE V. SCHOLARSHIPS AND GRANT PROGRAMS. SECTION 1. ACADEMIC SCHOLARSHIPS: 1.1 Dean's Lister Token Fee Exemption Grant: Awarded to both Makati and non-Makati residents who obtained a GWA within 1.00 to 1.75, with no grades lower than 2.00 in all academic courses and no grades lower than 2.50 in P.E. and NSTP during previous semester. Full token fee exemption: GWA within 1.00 to 1.25. Partial token fee exemption: GWA within 1.26 to 1.75. Requires at least one (1) semester in UMak College undergraduate level. Requirements: Filled out application form, Report of Grades from previous semester.

section: Article VI. Student Formation and Discipline (CSFD)
content: ARTICLE VI. STUDENT FORMATION AND DISCIPLINE. SECTION 1. STUDENT CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINE: University of Makati expects each student to behave in a manner manifesting moral integrity and personal refinement consistent with the true Heron's Student character. The Center for Student Formation and Discipline (CSFD) monitors and maintains proper conduct and discipline of students and puts them under its guidance at all times within and outside school premises.

section: Article VI. Section 3. Uniform and Dress Code Policy
content: SECTION 3. POLICIES ON UNIFORM AND EXEMPTION: 3.1 All students required to wear proper uniform specifically prescribed by college except during Wash Day (every Wednesday both for HSU and old students). 3.2 P.E. uniform worn during P.E. classes. 3.3 Identification cards (ID) must always be worn within school premises. 3.4 Prescribed shoes must be kept clean; no inappropriate footwear, e.g., slippers, step-ins. 3.6 Wearing of following NOT allowed inside campus: Male: Earrings, cap inside classrooms/offices, torn jeans, untidy hair, make-up, cross-dressing. Female: Multiple earrings, sleeveless/string blouse, plunging/tube blouse, torn jeans/leggings/jeggings, micro mini skirt/short-shorts, heavy make-up/noticeable dyed hair, rubber slippers. 3.7 Hair Code: Neat and tidy hair grooming, only subtle hair colors allowed.

section: Article VI. Section 3.8 & 3.9 Uniform Exemption & ID Confiscation
content: 3.8 Request for exemption from wearing prescribed uniform approved by Director of CSFD for: 3.8.1 Working Students, 3.8.2 On-the-Job Training Students, 3.8.3 Accident/Health-related Incidents, 3.8.4 During Activity Day. Pregnant students shall request certificate of exemption from CSFD. New students given grace period of two weeks from start of classes to secure uniform. 3.9 Identification Card: Wearing of ID card in campus is mandatory. Lost ID card reported immediately to CSFD. ID replacement fee paid at Cash Office. Confiscated ID or COR turned over to CSFD.

section: Article VI. Section 4.2 Major Offenses
content: SECTION 4.2 MAJOR OFFENSES: 4.2.13 Oral defamation; 4.2.14 Vandalism; 4.2.15 Lewdness; 4.2.16 Forging, falsifying or tampering of any academic or official records or documents; 4.2.18 Having somebody else take an examination for another; 4.2.19 Plagiarism; 4.2.20 Bribery; 4.2.21 Misappropriation of funds; 4.2.22 Hazing of any kind inflicted on students whether inside or outside campus; 4.2.23 Physical rumble, fist fighting, armed combat; 4.2.25 Direct physical assault upon students, faculty, admin staff; 4.2.26 Unauthorized collection (extortion) of money; 4.2.27 Theft; 4.2.28 Carrying firearms, deadly weapons, explosives; 4.2.33 Violation of Anti-Hazing Act of 2018 (RA 11053); 4.2.34 Dangerous drugs. Penalties: 1st Offense: Suspension; 2nd Offense: Exclusion/Dismissal/Non-Readmission/Expulsion.

section: Article VI. Process for Confiscated ID & SDC
content: PROCESS IN RELEASING CONFISCATED ID AND COR: Security personnel issues violation slip and turns over ID to CSFD. Student submits letter of apology with violation slip before ID is redeemed. Habitual violation of school policies warrants necessary disciplinary action. SECTION 5. THE STUDENT DISCIPLINARY COMMITTEE (SDC): SDC ensures proper conduct and discipline of students is implemented. Parent/guardian conference with CSFD required during investigation for major offenses. Procedures for suspension/dismissal/expulsion applied for habitual violators.

section: Tuition and Token Fee Exemption Basic Requirements
content: TUITION AND TOKEN FEE EXEMPTIONS: Basic Requirements: (1) Accomplished application form via OLEA / official UMak email; (2) Recent 2x2 colored ID picture; (3) Certificate of Registration (COR) for the current semester showing unpaid assessment; (4) Certificate of Good Moral Character; (5) No unexcused failing grades, Incomplete (INC), or Dropped marks (OD/UD) during the immediately preceding semester.

section: Dean's Lister Full and Partial Token Fee Exemption
content: DEAN'S LISTER SCHOLARSHIP: Full Token Fee Exemption (100% discount on tuition and token fees): Requires a General Weighted Average (GWA) of 1.00 to 1.25, with no grade lower than 2.00 in any academic course, and no grade lower than 2.50 in PE and NSTP. Partial Token Fee Exemption (50% discount): Requires a GWA of 1.26 to 1.75, with no grade lower than 2.00 in any academic course.

section: Student Assistant Token Fee Exemption
content: STUDENT ASSISTANT TOKEN FEE EXEMPTION: Full token fee discount granted to bonafide undergraduate students rendering authorized duty hours in academic colleges and administrative offices. Requirements: Written endorsement from the supervising office head or Dean, minimum cumulative GWA of 2.50, and certification of duty completion.

section: Varsity Athletes and Performing Artists Grants
content: UNIVERSITY VARSITY ATHLETES & PERFORMING ARTISTS: 100% tuition and token fee exemption granted to active members of the UMak Herons Varsity teams and the Center for Culture and the Arts (CCA) performing groups. Maintaining Requirements: Must carry at least 15 units, maintain a term GWA of 2.50 or better, with no failing marks.

section: College of Computing and Information Sciences (CCIS) Retention Rules
content: COLLEGE OF COMPUTING AND INFORMATION SCIENCES (CCIS). Retention Policy: To be retained in the Bachelor of Science in Computer Science (BSCS) or Bachelor of Science in Information Technology (BSIT) programs, students must maintain a General Weighted Average (GWA) of at least 2.25 in all major computing and programming subjects. Math Requirement: A minimum grade of 2.25 is required in Calculus and Discrete Structures.

section: CCIS Probation and Shifting Guidelines
content: Probation and Shifting: A student who fails two (2) major computing subjects in a single academic year is placed on College Probation. Incurring three (3) failing grades in major CCIS courses disqualifies the student from the BSCS and BSIT programs, requiring shifting to another college. Shifting Requirements: Cumulative GWA of 2.50 or better, endorsement from the CCIS Dean, and acceptance by the receiving college.

section: Campus Overview & Main Landmarks
content: UMAK CAMPUS DIRECTORY: The University of Makati campus is located along J.P. Rizal Extension, West Rembo, Taguig / Makati. Key facilities include: Administration Building, Academic Building 1, Academic Building 2, Academic Building 3, Higher Polytechnic Studies Building (HPSB 12-Story Tower), University Stadium, UMak Oval, and the University Gymnasium.

section: Administration Building Directory
content: ADMINISTRATION BUILDING DIRECTORY: Ground Floor (G/F): Office of the University Registrar (OUR), Center for Admission and Scholarship (CAS), Cashier / Cash Office, Accounting Office, Center for Student Services. 2nd Floor (2/F): Office of the University President, Board of Regents Boardroom, Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs (OVPAA). 3rd Floor (3/F): Office of the Vice President for Administration and Finance, Human Resource Management Office (HRMO), Legal Office.

section: Academic Building 3 and CIT Location
content: ACADEMIC BUILDING 3 DIRECTORY: Ground Floor (G/F): UMak Employees Multi-Purpose Cooperative, Audio-Visual Center. 2nd Floor (2/F): Center for Information Technology (CIT Office) located specifically at the South Wing, 2nd Floor. College of Computing and Information Sciences (CCIS) Dean's Office, Computer Laboratories 1 to 8. 3rd Floor (3/F): College of Engineering and Technology (CET) laboratories.

section: HPSB 12-Story Tower Directory
content: HIGHER POLYTECHNIC STUDIES BUILDING (HPSB): Ground Floor to 3rd Floor: University Library (Main Learning Resource Center), Law Library. 4th to 6th Floors: School of Law (SOL), College of Governance and Public Policy (CGPP). 7th to 9th Floors: Center of Imaging Health Sciences (CIHS), College of Allied Health Studies (CAHS), Nursing Simulation Laboratories. 10th to 12th Floors: Executive Suites, Conference Halls, University Auditorium.

section: Office of the University President
content: Office of the University President: University President: Prof. Charlemagne G. Laviña. Functions: Chief Executive Officer of the University. Administers university policies, represents the university in Board of Regents, exercises supervisory authority over all colleges, centers, and administrative units. Located at 2/F Administration Building.

section: Office of the University Registrar (OUR)
content: Office of the University Registrar (OUR): University Registrar: Ms. Cynthia Margaretta Rabago José. Functions: Student admission records, registration, enrollment verification, issuance of Transcript of Records (TOR), Certificate of Registration (COR), Honorable Dismissal, and graduation evaluations. Located at Ground Floor, Administration Building.

section: Center for Information Technology (CIT)
content: Center for Information Technology (CIT): Director: Engr. Ronald A. Polidario. Functions: Manages campus network infrastructure, student portal (OLEA), Online Report of Grades (OLROG), Scan-to-Pay integration, official student email provisioning (@umak.edu.ph), and campus cyber-security. Located at Academic Building 3, 2nd Floor, South Wing.
